title: Alpha-path averaged ridge on full features
hypothesis: Averaging ridge predictions over a fixed alpha path instead of selecting a single inner-CV alpha reduces selection variance and should generalize slightly better on the full bilateral feature set.

review.concerns: No test leakage: confound regression, bilateral averaging map, and StandardScaler are all fit on train.X only; the alpha path is fixed a priori and every prediction is deterministic (no RNG, no fold special-casing). Screen R2 0.085 / confirm 0.087 is well under the 0.12 'too good' line and the gain (t=2.16, p=0.018) is plausible. The main methodological caveat is not leakage but loss of adaptivity: dropping the nested CV also drops the raw-vs-averaged representation check, so if the name-based pairing is poor the model can no longer fall back to raw columns. Also the alpha grid caps at 1e4 and averages uniformly, which is an arbitrary prior (fine, but not validated).
review.insight: The win appears to come from variance reduction (smoothing over alphas) rather than a better feature representation, so the next idea should test whether the bilateral-average pairing still helps by comparing it head-to-head against raw columns under the same alpha-path averaging, and consider revisiting the alpha grid range instead of expanding the ensemble.
